column1: # Evidence behind CREDITS.md. One row per tracked file. Validated by scripts/check-provenance.sh.
# Keep that pin on its own line. --online reads the ECU commit with `grep -m1 '^# ecu=' | sed
# 's/.*(\([0-9a-f]\{40\}\)).*/\1/'`, and that leading `.*` is greedy: a second 40-hex parenthesis on
# the ecu= line wins, so --online clones ECU and tries to check out a Superpowers SHA that is not in
# that clone — git errors and the script dies under set -e. Measured. Guarded in
# tests/test-provenance-origins.sh, which nothing else would catch: no test runs --online.
# NOTE: README/LICENSE/CONTRIBUTING/CLAUDE.md/.gitignore share a path with ECU but are ours, not vendored.

Measured by executing every line against a live mcp-for-unity-server 3.4.5 on Unity 6000.0.68f1, 2026-08-14: start_session (lines 44 and 90), memory_snapshot and get_rendering_stats all answer success:false Unknown action, while get_frame_timing and get_counters on the same lines work and are untouched. Corrected to profiler_start, memory_take_snapshot and stats_get. The snapshot line states the com.unity.memoryprofiler precondition, because the real project this was measured on does not have that package and the fix would otherwise have traded one dead call for another. The prose under the fence records the failure shape that let all four survive -- an unknown action returns isError:false with success:false in the body -- so a reader learns why plausible names are not evidence. Guarded offline from now on by tests/test-mcp-citations.sh;live-bridge-task-1-r1: two corrections, both from executing the CORRECTED lines against the live editor. The com.unity.memoryprofiler precondition this file shipped one commit ago is FALSE and was never run: memory_take_snapshot wrote a 253,428-byte .snap into MemoryCaptures/ on a project whose manifest has no memoryprofiler (grep -c -> 0). The package supplies the analysis window, i.e. reading a snapshot, not taking one; the line now states the measurement, and says memory_compare_snapshots was NOT tested rather than asserting anything about it. The precondition came from the MCP server's own tool description and was written into the task brief as fact -- the same defect class this wave exists to fix, committed while fixing it. Second, get_counters as cited -- no parameters -- returns success:false with an EMPTY message, the least diagnosable of the five: category is required. The line now carries category:"Render" and notes that a category is large (Render 569 counters, Memory 44) and that the optional counters list is how to narrow it. get_counters had been classified 'resolves' by the same live sweep that condemned the four dead names, because the action NAME resolves and the CALL does not -- a distinction the prose under the fence now states, since it is the one tests/test-mcp-citations.sh structurally cannot make

anchored destructive-verb patterns to command position (start-of-line or after ;/&&/||/|) and bounded the verb-to-path gap to the same command segment, so text merely co-occurring with a path (JSON argument, unrelated chained command) no longer misclassifies as a destructive write (Defect 6); corrected the retry-affordance message to state byte-identical retry and print the recorded key (Defect 7); hardens echo|grep -q pipe against pipefail SIGPIPE fail-open on large content (here-string); 2026-08-13 surface-criterion O2: the five substring-anywhere patterns anchored or re-grounded so the gate stops blocking prose about a destructive command -- the three git verbs given the file's own CMD_START (plus the git -C/-c option forms, which were a false negative); find split out of the .meta deletion alternation and made to require an actual deletion action, since find alone lists; destructive SQL made to require a database client to be named, because CMD_START on SQL would have switched the classification off entirely; the C# member expression dropped as something no shell command position can hold, replaced by the two shapes that erase preferences from a shell; review round 1: the find clause required a deletion verb only, so the find route to a mass .meta RENAME went from blocked to allowed while this file's header and HOOK-REFERENCE.md both promise deletion or rename -- rename restored, and the verb now matched as a token so a path prefix, a git wrapper or a quote before it no longer hides it; git's global option forms extended past -c/-C, closing --git-dir; the closed-allowlist limit of the SQL client check and the macOS plist misclassification both named in comments rather than left to be rediscovered; re-review: restoring one rename verb restored one verb out of a family -- the find action arms now enumerate deletion (rm, unlink, shred, truncate) and rename (mv, rename, prename, mmv) instead of a single token each. Before this wave ANY find naming .meta was classified, which is why a count was blocked and also why every destructive verb was covered for free; requiring an action gave back the counts and dropped six acts with them, each measured blocked at be2a582 and allowed after. An enumerated verb list is a claim about what someone thought of, and that is recorded in the file rather than left implied; round 3 -- the find route stops enumerating harm. A hand-written denylist of destructive verbs was written three times and was incomplete every time; the decisive miss was perl-rename / file-rename, the same tool as prename under its other standard names, hidden by the same left-boundary mechanism the comment above it explained. The find shape is now decided by an ALLOWLIST of read-only commands: keep the action requirement (a count and a bare -print still pass), and once there is an exec'd command classify unless that command cannot modify what find hands it. The command is extracted by tokenising in bash rather than by regex, because the word after the introducer is a position and the regex attempts to express it are what kept missing verbs. One classification, meta-mutation, naming the command it saw rather than guessing deletion or rename -- the decision no longer depends on knowing the verb, so the message must not claim to.
